newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends lower on harvest activity, funds.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends lower on harvest activity, funds.

text.p: Fund selling amid prospects for an active weekend of harvesting in the U.S. Midwest pressed CBOT corn futures to a lower close, traders said.
"There is no mystery here. There's a good crop coming on. We dodged the bullet in the eastern corn belt from frost this week," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.

Corn held firm on the open but quickly sagged on the absence of speculative demand and the outlook for nearly ideal combining conditions in the key U.S. corn growing states. "There was a little support from the Sparks number but we are getting some hedge pressure," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Warm, dry weather over the weekend should ensure active harvesting of corn and soybeans in the U.S. Midwest, meteorologists said.

Traders said Sparks Companies released their estimate early Friday. The Memphis-based analytical firm pegged 1996 U.S. corn production at 8.955 billion bushels, slightly below some other private outlooks this week but above USDA's September forecast for 8.804 billion.
Corn closed 1-3/4 to 4-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with December down 2-1/2 at $2.89-1/2.
"I think we're trading a nine to 9.1 billion bushel crop at these levels," a trader said.
Fund selling totaled at least 20 million bushels with Griffin Trading the key seller of eight million bushels of December, the traders said.

Technicians said the corn market was oversold with the relative strength index (RSI) for December down to 12.412 at the close. An RSI of 20 or less is generally considered indicative of an oversold market.
December reached a session low of $2.89-1/2 per bushel, the lowest level for that month since $2.88-1/2 was touched on January 26.
December broke below support at $2.91 per bushel and ended just above the second support level of $2.88-1/2.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 60,000 contracts, up from 58,248 Thursday, according to the CBOT.
In corn options, FIMAT Futures bought 600 December $3.00 puts and sold 600 December $2.90 puts at 6 to 6-1/2 cents and Tenco Inc bought 500 December $2.70 puts at two cents, the traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 24,000 contracts, down from 25,949 Thursday.
